conviction_note: Eight small, mostly already-public items lean mildly positive (Q3 leasing pace, the 245 Park refinancing completing the $7.0B 2026 financing plan two days before the print, a tightening Manhattan market, a 17% / 12.5-day short) against a 17.9-point put skew on an unusable chain, a past-due 650 Fifth loan and an unsourced FFO bar with a $0.80 One Vanderbilt item of unknown quarter that can swing the headline either way; impact_sum +0.95 vs a scaled +0.21 (p_up 53 x abs 3.5) because the scaled number also carries the skew and the name's damped reaction history (Q2 beat plus $1.20 guide raise bought only +1.87%).
bar: Q3 2026 FFO/share: unsourced as FFO. The only Q3 figure found is a Benzinga 'non-GAAP EPS' consensus of $1.50 and revenue $177.0M (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/SLG/earnings-forecasts, search snippet only, page returned 403), which may or may not be FFO. Company guide: 2026 FFO $5.60-$5.90 (https://slgreen.com/sl-green-realty-corp-reports-second-quarter-2026-eps-of-0-38-per-share-and-ffo-of-1-43-per-share/, 2026-07-22); H1 FFO was $2.26 (Q1 $0.84, Q2 $1.43, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001040971/000162828026049346/a26q2supplemental.htm), so H2 needs ~$3.49 at the midpoint, including $0.80 of One Vanderbilt income whose quarter is not disclosed. If that $0.80 lands in Q3 the headline is ~$2.1+ against $1.50; if in Q4, Q3 is ~$1.35-1.50. Bar is unsourced/disputed, so every finding is capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest 12.2M shares, 17.1% of float, 12.5 days to cover, rising 7.6% m/m (equibles, page read 2026-10-21, settlement date not shown; https://equibles.com/stocks/SLG). Sweep row cites 23.8% of float (Benzinga sentiment, 2026-09-29) and 16.5% / 9.8 DTC (equibles, 2026-08-19): sources disagree but all put it at a crowded 16-24%. Insider net selling $2.3M over 90 days (one seller). Baseline: 25d skew +17.87 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 1.55, but ATM spread 165% of mid and total OI only 4,847, so the chain is a weak statement. Run-up -5.45% 20d, +2.64% 5d, 21% off 52w high.

findings.finding: SL Green said on 2026-09-14 that 2026 Manhattan office leasing reached 1,760,649 sq ft over 129 leases at +15.8% mark-to-market, against 1,374,425 sq ft at 2026-06-30, so ~386k sq ft were signed in Q3 by mid-September (vs 445k in all of Q2), and the pipeline rose to more than 1.0M sq ft (from ~900k in July); occupancy was 94.7% at 6/30 against a 95.0% year-end target.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (FFO $1.43 vs $1.19 consensus, leasing 445k sq ft at +18% MTM, FY guide raised $1.20) bought +1.87% (baseline 2026-07-23); Q1 2026 +6.05%; median abs reaction 1.87%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it is a company press release. What is not priced is the full-quarter number (Sep 14-30 signings) and whether occupancy crossed the 95% target early; if the market had priced a strong Q3 the stock would not be -5.45% over 20 days with puts bid.
findings.independence: CBRE Q3 2026 Manhattan figures (availability 13.7%, -290 bps y/y; net absorption +2.67M sq ft), https://www.cbre.com/insights/figures/manhattan-office-figures-q3-2026 — a market proxy, not SLG's own number.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-19, two days before the print, SLG refinanced 245 Park Avenue with a $2.0B five-year fixed-rate SASB CMBS at 6.52% (6.37% hedged SLG share), replacing $1.768B of mortgage and mezz debt, generating incremental liquidity and bringing its $7.0B 2026 financing plan 'to near completion'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print isolates a financing surprise; refinancing risk on 280 Park (Sept 2026 maturity) and 100 Church (Dec 2026) was the bear case. No reaction history on this line.
findings.why_not_priced: Released two sessions before the print, and the call is where management will quantify what the $7.0B plan has done to 2026-27 maturities (the 10-Q showed ~$4.37B due in rest-of-2026/2027 per a secondary read). If the market had priced the de-risking, the 20-day run-up would not be negative and put skew would not be 17.9 points. Financing question answered: the money refinances a 100%-leased asset and extends maturities, so it is not distress; the cost is a higher coupon whose prior rate is undisclosed, which may weigh slightly on FFO.
findings.independence: Disposition proceeds earmarked for unsecured debt repayment (110 Greene, https://slgreen.com/sl-green-announces-sale-of-110-greene-street-for-226-million/) point the same way; different document, same balance-sheet theme.

findings.finding: CBRE's Q3 2026 Manhattan office figures (published 2026-10-07): leasing 7.10M sq ft, 11% above the five-year quarterly average; availability 13.7%, down 70 bps q/q and 290 bps y/y; net absorption +2.67M sq ft; asking rent $80.40, +4% y/y. Colliers and Savills report ~10M sq ft on broader definitions.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None isolated; market reports are routine and SLG reactions have been damped (median 1.87%).
findings.why_not_priced: Public broker data; mostly priced. Only the transmission into SLG's own occupancy and rent spreads is unknown until the supplemental.
findings.independence: Proxy, not SLG's own number. CBRE also notes YTD leasing -5% y/y, which cuts the other way.

findings.finding: The Q2 release attributes $0.80/share of the 2026 FFO guide raise to 'additional income that will be recognized from One Vanderbilt Avenue' (SLG owns ~55%) without saying what it is or in which quarter it lands; H1 FFO was $2.26 against a $5.75 midpoint, so H2 needs ~$3.49 and the Q3 headline is either ~$2.1+ (item in Q3) or ~$1.35-1.50 (item in Q4) against a $1.50 snippet-only consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2025 FFO included $0.61 from the 522 Fifth repayment; the next reaction was -1.81% (2025-07-17). The market has looked through lumpy items on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: The timing is genuinely undisclosed, so no aggregator can carry a correct Q3 FFO consensus; a headline 'beat' or 'miss' driven by it is likely to be looked through, but screens may react at the open. Sign unknown, hence 0 with a wide band.
findings.independence: https://www.crowdfundedwealth.com/articles/sl-green-realty-slg-stock-dividend-ffo-2026 (2026-10-19) independently notes the filings do not disclose the item's nature or timing.

findings.finding: A 2026-10-19 read of the 10-Q reports the 650 Fifth Avenue loan matured in July 2026 and SLG is 'in discussions with the lender on resolution of the past maturity', a possible impairment / deed-in-lieu / write-off item in the Q3 print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: H1 2026 carried $35.2M of depreciable real estate reserves and impairments (10-Q, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001040971/000162828026054436/slg-20260630.htm) and Q1 2026 was bought +6.05%; impairments on non-core JVs have not driven reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: Disclosed in the 10-Q but not quantified; below FFO-relevant lines for a REIT (impairments are excluded from FFO), so sized at a fraction. Crowded short (17% of float) further shrinks a negative.
findings.independence: none (primary 10-Q text not reached in the excerpt fetched)

findings.finding: Dispositions: 110 Greene Street sold to Natora Group for $226.0M (2026-09-09, ~$216M net, Q4 close, to repay unsecured corporate debt), and 10 East 53rd Street ($312.2M, ~$100M net) was guided to close in Q3 2026 with no separate closing release on SLG's news page through 2026-10-21.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Asset-sale headlines have not been isolated as print drivers.
findings.why_not_priced: Public; mostly priced. The Q3 release will confirm whether 10 East 53rd closed on schedule (a slip would be a small negative).
findings.independence: 10 East 53rd timing from the Q2 release, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001040971/000162828026049346/a26q2earningsrelease.htm

findings.finding: Short interest of 12.2M shares, 17.1% of float, 12.5 days to cover and rising 7.6% month on month (equibles; Benzinga 23.8% on 2026-09-29), into a print where leasing and financing news is skewed positive.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 print +6.05% (largest of seven) came with leasing ahead and the stock depressed; otherwise reactions within ±2.3% except -4.12% in April 2025.
findings.why_not_priced: A crowded short is a mechanism rather than information: if positioning were neutral, put skew would not be 17.9 points and short interest would not be rising into a print after a $1.20 guide raise. The squeeze needs a non-negative print to fire.
findings.independence: Sweep row's Benzinga figure (23.8%, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/SLG/sentiment, 2026-09-29) and baseline put/call OI 1.55.
